knowledge.statement: With a configuration whose largest node id exceeds the number of nodes, the leader cannot advance the compacted index through `trim`. `LeaderState::with` allocates `accepted_indexes` for every id up to the largest one, phantom slots (ids that are not in the configuration) are never written, and `LeaderState::get_min_all_accepted_idx` minimises over that whole vector, so the reduced value is 0 no matter how far the real servers have decided. `SequencePaxos::trim` therefore computes a trim index of 0 for `trim(None)`, `InternalStorage::try_trim(0)` finds nothing to compact and the call returns `Ok(())` while `get_compacted_idx()` is unchanged; `trim(Some(k))` for any k >= 1 fails the guard `idx <= min_all_accepted_idx` and returns `CompactionErr::NotAllDecided(0)`, so the documented repair step ('users can retry with omni_paxos.trim(Some(idx)) which will then succeed') cannot succeed. Measured on real instances with nodes {1,2,3} versus {1,2,5}, one entry decided by every configured server: control compacted 0 -> 1, treatment stayed at 0 with `trim_none_result` = ok and `trim_explicit_result` = not_all_decided:0.
knowledge.conditions: Core crate with MemoryStorage, in-process lossless delivery, three servers, majority quorum, batch_size 1, one decided entry, leader node 1 in both cases. The trigger is any id set with a gap below the largest id (equivalently max_id > node count): {1,2,5} was executed, {2,3,4} or {1,3} follow from the same sizing and were not executed. Snapshot-based compaction is not affected by the reduced value (`try_snapshot` uses the decided index) and remains available as a workaround; decision counting is not affected either, because `is_chosen` only counts slots whose accepted index is at least the candidate index and phantom slots hold 0.

interpretations.rationale: Current account. `LeaderState::with` allocates one accepted-index slot per id up to the largest id in the configuration, and `LeaderState::get_min_all_accepted_idx` reduces over that whole vector instead of over the configured servers, so any id set with a phantom slot below the largest id pins the reduced value at 0 however far the real servers have decided. `SequencePaxos::trim` compares the caller-supplied index against that reduced value and then asks `InternalStorage::try_trim` to compact; the measured control shows the intended behaviour (nodes {1,2,3}, one entry decided by all three, `trim(None)` returned `ok` and moved the compacted index 0 -> 1) while the treatment (nodes {1,2,5}, same state: all servers decided, `decided_idx_before_trim` 1) is evaluated `violated` with valid witness index 3: `trim(None)` reported `ok` with the compacted index still 0, and the documented repair `trim(Some(1))` returned `NotAllDecided(0)` because the guard requires an index at or below the reduced value of 0. Two consequences follow for a legal configuration: the trim API silently reports success while making no progress, and the log can then only be compacted by snapshotting, so the documented 'highest trimmable index' semantics and the documented retry path both fail. Configuration is accepted by the target's own validation (`ClusterConfig::validate` requires only more than one node, a non-zero configuration id, valid quorums and that the node set contains this server's pid; the docs and existing suites never state or use contiguous ids), so the configuration's own producer admits the state that the trim consumer mishandles. The trigger generalises to any id set with a gap below the maximum (for instance {2,3,4} or {1,3}); that generalisation is derived from the sizing code and was not executed. The scope is progress/availability of trimming, not safety: `is_chosen` counts only slots whose accepted index reaches the candidate index and phantom slots hold 0, so decision formation is unaffected, and `try_snapshot` uses the decided index rather than the reduced value, so snapshotting still compacts.
counterevidence: Trimming is optional compaction: the cluster keeps making progress and the log stays correct, so the defect costs unbounded log growth and a misleading success return rather than lost work.
`try_snapshot` does not consult the reduced value, so a caller that snapshots (with or without `local_only`) can compact under the same configuration; the defect is confined to the trim path.

The probe used MemoryStorage and a lossless in-process transport; a storage backend that refuses the no-op trim or a network that changes the timing could alter the observed surface, though the reduced value is computed in the core and does not depend on storage.
Only one sparse id set ({1,2,5}) was executed; the generalisation to other gapped sets rests on the sizing code, not on measurement.
limitations: Three servers, one decided entry, batch_size 1, majority quorum, node 1 leading in both cases; larger clusters or logs with several entries are unmeasured (the reduced value does not depend on either, but the probe does not demonstrate that).
No snapshot or trim-with-snapshot case was run, so the claim that snapshotting remains available is source-derived from `try_snapshot`/`InternalStorage`, not measured here.

The `trim_explicit_result` in the control was `ok` with no further compaction (the index was already compacted by the preceding `trim(None)`), so the control confirms only that `trim(None)` compacts and that a later explicit call at that index is accepted.

knowledge.statement: `ActorState::drain_notifiers` resolves a pending `append_notify` in a fixed arm order: a pending whose recorded assignment satisfies `assigned_idx <= local decided index` is answered `Ok(assigned_idx)` first; only when that does not hold and the ballot recorded at assignment is lower than the node's current promise is `Err(AppendError::Superseded { log_entry_idx: assigned_idx })` sent; otherwise the deadline arm `now > deadline` yields `Err(Timeout)` and unsettled pendings are retained for the next tick. The `Ok` arm compares only the index against the local decided index, with the assignment ballot and the entry's identity unused.
knowledge.conditions: Applies while the actor loop's tick branch runs and the pending entry has `assigned = Some((idx, ballot))`; the node's local decided index is read from the same `OmniPaxos` instance as the promise ballot used by the `Superseded` arm.

knowledge.statement: In this actor layer an assignment is only the pair `(log index, ballot in effect at assignment)`; `Pending::assigned: Option<(usize, Ballot)>` and `record_assignment(id, idx, ballot)` store no value, digest or entry id that could be compared against the entry actually stored at `idx` in the decided log. An index recorded through `append_tracked` (local accept as leader) or through `AsyncRuntimeMsg::Assigned` (leader reply) is therefore indistinguishable, from the completion signal alone, from a later different entry decided at the same index.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to `append_notify` completion on the origin actor, for assignments produced by the leader-side immediate accept path and by the leader's `Assigned` reply; `EntryId` identifies the caller's *pending call*, never the log slot's content.

knowledge.statement: A node that is leader and in `Phase::Accept` advances its own accepted index as soon as it appends an entry locally; entries are replicated afterwards by `AcceptDecide`/`Accepted` and only a write-quorum of reported accepted indexes makes an index chosen (`LeaderState::is_chosen` counts accepted indexes against the accept quorum). Consequently a locally accepted index can exist in the leader's log without any follower holding it, and a subsequent leader adopts only the log of the promise with the highest `(n_accepted, accepted_idx)` via `InternalStorage::sync_log`, which can replace that index with a different value.
knowledge.conditions: Applies with the majority or flexible quorum configured for the cluster, when the replication messages of that index do not reach a write quorum before leadership changes; it does not apply to an index already chosen by a write quorum, which a new leader must retain.

knowledge.statement: For the same lost-entry state, the resolution delivered to `append_notify` differs by tick granularity. Retained run of the three-case probe: mode A (no partition, 2 ms ticks) resolved `ok` with the caller's entry at the returned index; mode B (leader partitioned from both followers, entry accepted only locally, new leader on node 3 decides a different entry at the same index, 2 ms ticks) resolved `superseded` with the origin's decided index still 0 and no decided entries readable; mode C (identical setup, 80 ms ticks) resolved `ok(assigned_idx = 1)` while the origin's decided log at index 1 held the new leader's entry and the caller's entry appeared in no decided log (`entry_equals_submitted` false, origin decided values `22`, origin decided index 1, origin leader pid 3, origin decided index 0 while partitioned).
knowledge.conditions: Three-node cluster, majority quorum, batch_size 1, node 1 the pre-partition leader, message loss modelled as dropped whole messages in an in-process in-memory transport, no node restart (the origin is re-synchronized in-process). The `ok` arm is delivered when the origin's promise change and its decided-index advance both fall inside one tick period; with a tick period near the Prepare/AcceptSync round trip the `superseded` arm is delivered instead. Both arms were observed under this same setup, so neither is a property of the lost-entry state alone.

knowledge.statement: The repository's own caller of `append_notify` treats a successful resolution as synchronous durability confirmation of that specific entry and announces the returned index without re-reading the log at it: `examples/kv_store_async/src/main.rs` documents `append_notify` as being for "a specific entry whose durability the caller must confirm synchronously ... the entry is decided at its assigned index", and after `append_notify(quota).await?` it prints "quota entry durably decided at log idx {idx}, safe to announce". The existing runtime test for the same call asserts only that the returned index is non-zero and that the decided suffix is non-empty, so no in-repo test pins the entry actually occupying the returned index.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to callers that follow the documented/example pattern of treating `Ok(idx)` as confirmation for their own entry at `idx` without reading the decided log at that index. Under the mode-C interleaving of the retained executions (leader partitioned, entry accepted locally, new leader decides a different entry at the same index, origin re-synchronized) that pattern turns the false success into an announced write that is not in the decided log.
